contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #184: Correspondence coloring with a fixed forbidden subgraph.

Audit the independence manuscript weighted-triangle theorem on every finite simple graph with arbitrary positive vertex weights, and distinguish its global structural proof from the coloring-specific localized adaptation.

definitions.cross_mass: For every real x>=1 and every A,B with w(A),w(B)<=exp(x), the directed sum e_w(A,B) is at most C*w(A)*(x+max(0,log(1/w(A)))); its value is zero for A empty. Overlap is permitted.
definitions.scope: No minimum weight, normalization, optimizer, or forbidden-clique hypothesis is assumed for the global structural theorem. Coloring locality and participation are separate open obligations.

contexts.statement: Polynomial-logarithmic extension of weighted triangle mass from hereditary directed cross mass on arbitrary finite simple positive-weighted graphs.

definitions.H_p_C: For every real x>=p and every U,V with w(U),w(V)<=exp(x), e_w(U,V)<=C*w(U)*(x+max(0,log(1/w(U))))^p, with zero at empty U; p is an integer >=1, C>=1, and sets may overlap.
definitions.certification_boundary: The full graph theorem is proved in prose for independent review. Main.lean formalizes only the separately stated universal algebraic core, not the entropy support argument or the entire graph theorem.

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 184 (Correspondence coloring with a fixed forbidden subgraph.; papers: Correspondence coloring graphs with a forbidden clique; A logarithmic independence bound for clique-free graphs; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/184.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.
For every C>=1 there is a constant C_triangle(C) such that every finite simple positive-weighted graph satisfying full cross_mass has T<=C_triangle(C)*M, uniformly in graph order and all weights.
A weight-preserving homomorphism injective on directed edges preserves cross_mass and does not increase M, T, or projected neighborhood mass.
For arbitrary positive weights, sum_edges w_u*w_v*c_uv=3T and sum_u w_u*h_u=6T; successive deletion of edges with current c_uv<tau loses at most tau*M.

Under cross_mass, x>=32, s_u<=exp(x), and c_uv>=1/x on every edge, K_u^j=P_u*((I+P_u)/2)^j has density <=x*w_y and average entropy -log x<=H_0<=...<=H_ceil(x)<=(10+42C^2+2C)*log x. A single shared j has triangle-averaged adjacent-row TV <=2*sqrt(11+42C^2+2C)*sqrt(log(x)/x).
For these triangle-biased reversible kernels, the average probability of K_u(y,v)<w_v*exp(-sqrt(x)) is <=(A_C+1)*log(x)/(sqrt(x)+log(x)), without a minimum weight.

These kernels admit a finite shared-label coupling yielding an edge-injective weight-preserving split graph with all neighborhoods <=exp(sqrt(x)) and retained triangle mass >=(1-a_C*log(x)/sqrt(x))*T.
Peeling at 1/x and square-root neighborhood reduction have uniformly summable multiplicative and additive losses, giving T<=2*(1+exp(X(C))/3)*M with X depending only on C.
The independence manuscript claims every variational maximizing weight vector on a nonempty finite K_r-free graph satisfies cross_mass with C=16*r^2.
Optimizer cross_mass together with the structural weighted-triangle theorem supplies T<=B_r*M in the independence argument; these two inputs alone do not verify its entire main theorem.
The coloring sparse mean-one multiplier and dual argument supplies its priced local cross estimate with additive error and locality and per-part participation hypotheses.
The coloring local cross estimate transfers through directed-edge-injective splitting with the stated locality and per-part hypotheses.
The coloring-specific entropy, reverse qualification and iterative splitting arguments control priced triangle mass with the claimed radius, participation, and additive errors.
The coloring priced triangle bound closes the dual target for the adjustment lemma, including its listed-support participation bound; this is the input used by correspondence-coloring rounds.
A mathematical refutation consists of a fully admissible witness to a literal false intermediate assertion, or one fixed-C family satisfying full cross_mass and with T/M unbounded.

For every integer p>=1 and C>=1, every finite simple graph with arbitrary positive vertex weights satisfying H_p_C has T<=2*(1+exp(X)/3)*M with constants as defined in the context. The exponent-one case verifies the manuscript weighted-triangle theorem.
For every integer p>=1 and every x>=p, g_p_x is nondecreasing. Hence H_p_C is preserved under weight-preserving homomorphisms injective on directed edges.

For every integer p>=1, C>=1 and x>=max(32,(p+6)^2), H_p_C together with s_u<=exp(x) and c_uv>=1/x yields H_R<=(3p+7+C^2*42^p+C*2^p)*log x and one common time with averaged adjacent-row TV <=2*sqrt(A+1)*sqrt(log(x)/x).

Under H_p_C and the stated local-walk hypotheses, finite simultaneous coupling and reversed-row qualification give a directed-edge-injective split with neighborhoods <=exp(sqrt(x)) and retained triangle mass >=(1-a*log(x)/sqrt(x))*T. Peeling extends this to arbitrary bounded neighborhoods with additive loss M/x.

For X=(16*a*(p+6))^4, square-root iteration has total multiplicative loss <=1/2 and reciprocal-parameter sum <=1, independently of length and initial scale. Its terminal normalization implies the universal polynomial-profile triangle bound.

For every pair of integers 1<=q<p, the single-edge weighted graph with weights 2^(-n), n^p for every integer n>=max(4,p^2) satisfies H_p_C with fixed C=2^p, whereas every exponent-q cross constant is at least 2^(-q)*n^(p-q).

For arbitrary finite index types and real sequences, detailed balance exchanges two-coordinate expectations; a shifted lower and mean bound imply the strict-tail probability bound; halving controls all finite partial sums; the specified nonnegative-loss recurrence and terminal inequality imply the uniform mass bound. For all natural exponents the endpoint and profile-separation power inequalities hold, with exactly the hypotheses of Main.lean.
claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

namespace TriangleAudit

theorem reversible_swap {I : Type*} [Fintype I]
    (pi : I → ℝ) (K f : I → I → ℝ)
    (balance : ∀ v y, pi v * K v y = pi y * K y v) :
    (∑ v, ∑ y, pi v * K v y * f v y) =
      ∑ v, ∑ y, pi v * K v y * f y v := by
  calc
    (∑ v, ∑ y, pi v * K v y * f v y) =
        ∑ y, ∑ v, pi v * K v y * f v y := Finset.sum_comm
    _ = ∑ y, ∑ v, pi y * K y v * f v y := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro y _
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro v _
      rw [balance v y]
    _ = ∑ v, ∑ y, pi v * K v y * f y v := rfl

theorem averaged_cutoff {I : Type*} [Fintype I]
    (prob ell : I → ℝ) (b t H : ℝ)
    (hp : ∀ i, 0 ≤ prob i) (htotal : ∑ i, prob i = 1)
    (hlower : ∀ i, -b ≤ ell i)
    (hmean : ∑ i, prob i * ell i ≤ H) :
    (t + b) * (∑ i, if t < ell i then prob i else 0) ≤ H + b := by
  classical
  calc
    (t + b) * (∑ i, if t < ell i then prob i else 0) =
        ∑ i, if t < ell i then (t + b) * prob i else 0 := by
      simp only [Finset.mul_sum, mul_ite, mul_zero]
    _ ≤ ∑ i, prob i * (ell i + b) := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro i _
      by_cases hi : t < ell i
      · simp only [hi, ite_true]
        have hprod := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (le_of_lt hi) (hp i)
        nlinarith
      · simp only [hi, ite_false]
        apply mul_nonneg (hp i)
        linarith [hlower i]
    _ = (∑ i, prob i * ell i) + b := by
      simp_rw [mul_add]
      rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.sum_mul, htotal, one_mul]
    _ ≤ H + b := add_le_add_right hmean b

theorem averaged_cutoff_probability {I : Type*} [Fintype I]
    (prob ell : I → ℝ) (b t H : ℝ)
    (hp : ∀ i, 0 ≤ prob i) (htotal : ∑ i, prob i = 1)
    (hlower : ∀ i, -b ≤ ell i)
    (hmean : ∑ i, prob i * ell i ≤ H) (hdenom : 0 < t + b) :
    (∑ i, if t < ell i then prob i else 0) ≤ (H + b) / (t + b) := by
  classical
  apply (le_div_iff₀ hdenom).2
  simpa only [mul_comm] using averaged_cutoff prob ell b t H hp htotal hlower hmean

theorem halving_sum (e : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hnonneg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ e i)
    (hhalf : ∀ i, e (i + 1) ≤ e i / 2) (n : ℕ) :
    (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, e i) ≤ 2 * e 0 := by
  have stronger : ∀ k, (∑ i ∈ Finset.range k, e i) + 2 * e k ≤ 2 * e 0 := by
    intro k
    induction k with
    | zero => simp
    | succ k ih =>
      rw [Finset.sum_range_succ]
      linarith [hhalf k]
  have htail : 0 ≤ 2 * e n := mul_nonneg (by norm_num) (hnonneg n)
  linarith [stronger n]

theorem telescoping_loss (T eps b : ℕ → ℝ) (M0 : ℝ)
    (hstep : ∀ i, T i ≤ T (i + 1) + eps i * T 0 + b i * M0) (n : ℕ) :
    T 0 ≤ T n + T 0 * (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, eps i) +
      M0 * (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, b i) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
    rw [Finset.sum_range_succ, Finset.sum_range_succ]
    nlinarith [hstep n]

theorem bounded_mass_iteration (T M eps b : ℕ → ℝ) (L : ℝ) (n : ℕ)
    (hT0 : 0 ≤ T 0) (hM0 : 0 ≤ M 0)
    (heps : ∀ i, 0 ≤ eps i) (hb : ∀ i, 0 ≤ b i)
    (hTle : ∀ i, T i ≤ T 0) (hMle : ∀ i, M i ≤ M 0)
    (hrec : ∀ i, (1 - eps i) * T i - b i * M i ≤ T (i + 1))
    (hsumeps : (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, eps i) ≤ 1 / 2)
    (hsumb : (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, b i) ≤ 1)
    (hterminal : 3 * T n ≤ L * M 0) :
    T 0 ≤ 2 * (1 + L / 3) * M 0 := by
  have hstep : ∀ i, T i ≤ T (i + 1) + eps i * T 0 + b i * M 0 := by
    intro i
    have he := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hTle i) (heps i)
    have hm := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hMle i) (hb i)
    nlinarith [hrec i]
  have htel := telescoping_loss T eps b (M 0) hstep n
  have he := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hsumeps hT0
  have hm := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hsumb hM0
  nlinarith

theorem small_endpoint_bound (n x ell : ℝ) (p : ℕ)
    (hn : 0 ≤ n) (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hell : 1 / 2 ≤ ell) :
    n ^ p ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ p * (x + n * ell) ^ p := by
  have hprod : 0 ≤ n * (ell - 1 / 2) :=
    mul_nonneg hn (sub_nonneg.mpr hell)
  have hbase : n ≤ 2 * (x + n * ell) := by nlinarith
  have hp := pow_le_pow_left₀ hn hbase p
  simpa only [mul_pow] using hp

theorem profile_separation (n ell : ℝ) (p q : ℕ)
    (hn : 0 ≤ n) (hell : ell ≤ 1) (hpq : q ≤ p)
    (hbase_nonneg : 0 ≤ n + n * ell) :
    (n + n * ell) ^ q * n ^ (p - q) ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ q * n ^ p := by
  have hprod : 0 ≤ n * (1 - ell) :=
    mul_nonneg hn (sub_nonneg.mpr hell)
  have hbase : n + n * ell ≤ 2 * n := by nlinarith
  have hp := pow_le_pow_left₀ hbase_nonneg hbase q
  have hsum : q + (p - q) = p := by omega
  calc
    (n + n * ell) ^ q * n ^ (p - q) ≤
        (2 * n) ^ q * n ^ (p - q) :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hp (pow_nonneg hn _)
    _ = (2 : ℝ) ^ q * (n ^ q * n ^ (p - q)) := by rw [mul_pow]; ring
    _ = (2 : ℝ) ^ q * n ^ p := by rw [← pow_add, hsum]

end TriangleAudit

import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

namespace TriangleAudit

theorem reversible_swap {I : Type*} [Fintype I]

      ∑ v, ∑ y, pi v * K v y * f y v := by

    (∑ v, ∑ y, pi v * K v y * f v y) =
        ∑ y, ∑ v, pi v * K v y * f v y := Finset.sum_comm
    _ = ∑ y, ∑ v, pi y * K y v * f v y := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro y _
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro v _
      rw [balance v y]

    (prob ell : I → ℝ) (b t H : ℝ)
    (hp : ∀ i, 0 ≤ prob i) (htotal : ∑ i, prob i = 1)
    (hlower : ∀ i, -b ≤ ell i)
    (hmean : ∑ i, prob i * ell i ≤ H) :
    (t + b) * (∑ i, if t < ell i then prob i else 0) ≤ H + b := by
  classical
  calc
    (t + b) * (∑ i, if t < ell i then prob i else 0) =
        ∑ i, if t < ell i then (t + b) * prob i else 0 := by
      simp only [Finset.mul_sum, mul_ite, mul_zero]
    _ ≤ ∑ i, prob i * (ell i + b) := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro i _
      by_cases hi : t < ell i
      · simp only [hi, ite_true]
        have hprod := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (le_of_lt hi) (hp i)
        nlinarith
      · simp only [hi, ite_false]
        apply mul_nonneg (hp i)
        linarith [hlower i]
    _ = (∑ i, prob i * ell i) + b := by
      simp_rw [mul_add]
      rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.sum_mul, htotal, one_mul]
    _ ≤ H + b := by linarith

theorem averaged_cutoff_probability {I : Type*} [Fintype I]
    (prob ell : I → ℝ) (b t H : ℝ)
    (hp : ∀ i, 0 ≤ prob i) (htotal : ∑ i, prob i = 1)
    (hlower : ∀ i, -b ≤ ell i)
    (hmean : ∑ i, prob i * ell i ≤ H) (hdenom : 0 < t + b) :
    (∑ i, if t < ell i then prob i else 0) ≤ (H + b) / (t + b) := by
  classical
  apply (le_div_iff₀ hdenom).2
  simpa only [mul_comm] using averaged_cutoff prob ell b t H hp htotal hlower hmean

theorem halving_sum (e : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hnonneg : ∀ i, 0 ≤ e i)
    (hhalf : ∀ i, e (i + 1) ≤ e i / 2) (n : ℕ) :
    (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, e i) ≤ 2 * e 0 := by
  have stronger : ∀ k, (∑ i ∈ Finset.range k, e i) + 2 * e k ≤ 2 * e 0 := by
    intro k
    induction k with
    | zero => simp
    | succ k ih =>
      rw [Finset.sum_range_succ]
      linarith [hhalf k]
  have htail : 0 ≤ 2 * e n := mul_nonneg (by norm_num) (hnonneg n)
  linarith [stronger n]

theorem telescoping_loss (T eps b : ℕ → ℝ) (M0 : ℝ)
    (hstep : ∀ i, T i ≤ T (i + 1) + eps i * T 0 + b i * M0) (n : ℕ) :
    T 0 ≤ T n + T 0 * (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, eps i) +
      M0 * (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, b i) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
    rw [Finset.sum_range_succ, Finset.sum_range_succ]
    nlinarith [hstep n]

theorem bounded_mass_iteration (T M eps b : ℕ → ℝ) (L : ℝ) (n : ℕ)
    (hT0 : 0 ≤ T 0) (hM0 : 0 ≤ M 0)
    (heps : ∀ i, 0 ≤ eps i) (hb : ∀ i, 0 ≤ b i)
    (hTle : ∀ i, T i ≤ T 0) (hMle : ∀ i, M i ≤ M 0)
    (hrec : ∀ i, (1 - eps i) * T i - b i * M i ≤ T (i + 1))
    (hsumeps : (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, eps i) ≤ 1 / 2)
    (hsumb : (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, b i) ≤ 1)
    (hterminal : 3 * T n ≤ L * M 0) :
    T 0 ≤ 2 * (1 + L / 3) * M 0 := by
  have hstep : ∀ i, T i ≤ T (i + 1) + eps i * T 0 + b i * M 0 := by
    intro i
    have he := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hTle i) (heps i)
    have hm := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hMle i) (hb i)
    nlinarith [hrec i]
  have htel := telescoping_loss T eps b (M 0) hstep n
  have he := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hsumeps hT0
  have hm := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hsumb hM0
  nlinarith

theorem small_endpoint_bound (n x ell : ℝ) (p : ℕ)
    (hn : 0 ≤ n) (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hell : 1 / 2 ≤ ell) :
    n ^ p ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ p * (x + n * ell) ^ p := by
  have hprod : 0 ≤ n * (ell - 1 / 2) :=
    mul_nonneg hn (sub_nonneg.mpr hell)
  have hbase : n ≤ 2 * (x + n * ell) := by nlinarith
  have hp := pow_le_pow_left₀ hn hbase p
  simpa only [mul_pow] using hp

theorem profile_separation (n ell : ℝ) (p q : ℕ)
    (hn : 0 ≤ n) (hell : ell ≤ 1) (hpq : q ≤ p)
    (hbase_nonneg : 0 ≤ n + n * ell) :
    (n + n * ell) ^ q * n ^ (p - q) ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ q * n ^ p := by
  have hprod : 0 ≤ n * (1 - ell) :=
    mul_nonneg hn (sub_nonneg.mpr hell)
  have hbase : n + n * ell ≤ 2 * n := by nlinarith
  have hp := pow_le_pow_left₀ hbase_nonneg hbase q
  have hsum : q + (p - q) = p := by omega
  calc
    (n + n * ell) ^ q * n ^ (p - q) ≤
        (2 * n) ^ q * n ^ (p - q) :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hp (pow_nonneg hn _)
    _ = (2 : ℝ) ^ q * (n ^ q * n ^ (p - q)) := by rw [mul_pow]; ring
    _ = (2 : ℝ) ^ q * n ^ p := by rw [← pow_add, hsum]

end TriangleAudit
